Hi Sarah / Tom,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great call. Quick recap and next steps so we have shared alignment on integration and priorities.

Recap (from our discovery):
- Primary use case: in-product contextual search + reranking for enterprise docs, with two inference paths: low-latency chat and batched embedding/recall + reranker.
- Requirements: private networking support (VPC peering), SSO-based provisioning, and clear cost/latency controls for preview vs. production.
- Initial target: prototype SDK integration (Python/TS), local testing, then Dedicated staging run for load tests.

Immediate next steps (owner):
1) SDK quickstart + env setup: I attached the quickstart bundle and a one-page setup diagram. Start with the Python sample (recommended for your backend) and the TypeScript example for your front-end integration. (Owner: TechFin)
2) Auth & service accounts: we recommend service account + short-lived credentials for server components; we can provide a scoped service principal for your staging project. (Owner: Redwood - Marissa / Dev)
3) Routing & model variants: we'll show how to pin the chat path to a low-latency variant and route batch jobs (embeddings/rerank) to cost-optimized nodes. (Owner: Redwood - Aditya)
4) Evals/QA: share a small prompt set and sample documents; we'll run a smoke evaluation and alert on regressions. (Owner: TechFin + Redwood)

Resources attached / links:
- redwood-sdk-quickstart.zip (contains python/ts samples, dockerfile, local test harness)
- architecture-diagram.png (one-page network + routing)
- Quickstart repo: https://github.com/redwoodinc/sdk-quickstart

If you want, we can run a 45-minute integration session this week to walk through the sample app and wire up auth. Proposed times: Wed 9–11am PT or Thu 1–3pm PT.

Thanks — looking forward to getting you on a dev loop.

Sarah — good questions, answered inline below. Also pasted minimal snippets for Python/TS quickstart to make the first run fast.

1) Embeddings + reranker guidance:
- Batch sizing: for CPU/light-GPU local testing, use batches of 32–64 documents. For Dedicated staging on GPU pools, we typically use 256–1024 depending on seq length and quantization. Start conservative and increase until throughput/latency SLOs are met.
- Pipeline pattern:
  a) Offline index: run embeddings job to generate vectors and store in your vector DB (we've included an example 3-stage pipeline in the quickstart README).
  b) Online rerank: retrieve top-N by vector similarity, then call reranker model (structured output) for final scoring. We recommend top-100 -> rerank to top-10.

2) Local testing w/ small model: yes. The quickstart Dockerfile includes a minimal config that uses a CPU-optimized tiny model (quantized) so you can run the runtime locally without GPUs. See ./local/README.md in the zip.

3) Auth for CI (GitHub Actions): two options:
- Short-lived key via service account: we create a scoped service account for your CI, issue a short-lived token (rotated). Actions can use the token via repo secrets.
- API key with ingress restrictions: if you prefer keys, we recommend IP / VPC restrictions + reduced scope.

Python quickstart (run locally):
- Install: pip install redwood-sdk
- Example:
  from redwood_sdk import RedwoodClient
  client = RedwoodClient(api_key="$REDWOOD_API_KEY")
  # simple chat
  resp = client.chat.create(model="redwood-chat-1", input="Summarize the incident notes")
  print(resp.text)

TypeScript quickstart (front-end + node):
- npm install @redwoodinc/sdk
- Node example:
  import { RedwoodClient } from '@redwoodinc/sdk'
  const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY })
  const resp = await client.chat.create({ model: 'redwood-chat-1', input: 'Extract entities' })
  console.log(resp.output)

Notes on structured output / tool calling:
- The SDK supports structured output schemas and tool calling out-of-the-box. For rerankers, we recommend returning JSON with scores and metadata to simplify downstream ranking logic.
- We'll provide a small set of schema examples in the repo (openapi-style).

I've also added a short checklist below to accelerate your first run:
- [ ] Unzip quickstart, run docker-compose up (local runtime + sample app)
- [ ] Set REDWOOD_API_KEY in your local env or use the local service-account token script
- [ ] Run sample embedding job: python samples/embed_docs.py --input sample_docs/
- [ ] Run reranker smoke test: node samples/rerank_demo.js

See attached quickstart + links: https://github.com/redwoodinc/sdk-quickstart

Adding a few practical implementation notes for the integration session (I can demo each):

Auth details:
- We'll provision a service account with scoped permissions: embeddings:write, embeddings:read, chat:invoke. Tokens are short-lived (1h) and we provide a refresh endpoint. For GH Actions we provide a token minting helper script (samples/ci/mint_token.sh).

Routing & models:
- Use route policies to send latency-sensitive /chat requests to the low-latency cluster in us-west and batch/embeddings to cost-optimized nodes (us-central). Example route config in quickstart/config/routes.yaml.
- You can pin model variants per route; fallback policy is automatic to the next compatible variant if capacity is constrained.

Local runtime tips:
- The quickstart Docker has two profiles: local-small (CPU quantized) and local-gpu. For Windows / Mac M1 we recommend running the local-small container with 2–4 CPUs and 4GB RAM for smoke tests.

I'll bring the mint_token.sh demo and the route config snippet to the call.

Cheers,
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

One more note on the reranker and structured outputs before the call:

- Reranker pattern: retrieve top-100 via embeddings vector search, call the reranker with a structured schema that returns {score: float, explanation: string, match_span: {start:int,end:int}}. Keep the reranker model smaller and focused on scoring + extraction to reduce cost.
- A/B approach: run a canary rerank route for 10% traffic to compare production variant to new model. SDK supports per-route eval hooks to capture metrics.
- If you'd like, we can prepare a short eval set using 200 sample queries and run a before/after to quantify delta.

Next step: Marissa, confirm Wed 10am PT invite (Sarah) and I'll prepare the rerank demo + a short Jupyter notebook showing embedding indexing throughput.

- Aditya
